### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`  _(via DelegatedAdminGate (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via DelegatedAdminGate (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **219** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **17** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7b2bb668dacc8d915c161791facf20be78138a99` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a75819f70b5f3159cc9aeec788129b3d2655dbf1` — the merge of head `51d9481a50435663746886fd79a8bca4aaed02f7` into base `7b2bb668dacc8d915c161791facf20be78138a99`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a75819f70b5f3159cc9aeec788129b3d2655dbf1 && git checkout a75819f70b5f3159cc9aeec788129b3d2655dbf1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7b2bb668dacc8d915c161791facf20be78138a99 51d9481a50435663746886fd79a8bca4aaed02f7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7b2bb668dacc8d915c161791facf20be78138a99 && git merge --no-ff 51d9481a50435663746886fd79a8bca4aaed02f7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7b2bb668dacc8d915c161791facf20be78138a99
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7b2bb668dacc8d915c161791facf20be78138a99` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `51d9481a50435663746886fd79a8bca4aaed02f7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/org-admin-assignment-boundary.posture.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/org-admin-assignment-removal-unreadable-row.dogfood.test.ts, .changeset/org-admin-removal-caller-read.md + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts (`readDoorAnswerForGateRefusal`, the gate call, step 2.7), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (`getCallerPreImage`, `absentUnderCallerRead`, the gate's construction), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-addressed-writes.ts (`readRowById`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-object-admission.ts (the admission probe's call into the gate), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts (the two organization-administrator sets), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-position.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`findOne`), packages/spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts, content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx

Reviewed on the net diff against `main` at the merge base (4 files, +319/−2), the PR body and the head's check-runs; no dispatch order and no developer report were read as inputs. The record stays at rule level.

### ① Derived judgments

**What changes, and for whom.** One thing: in the ORGANIZATION branch of the ADR-0090 D12 gate, the pre-image of a by-id removal is now the caller's own by-id read through the engine (`organizationTargets`) instead of a system-context read. The read has the same shape as the by-id write doors' own pre-image read (`readRowById`: `findOne(object, { where: { id }, context })`), so it is the read door's own question, every wall and read visibility included.

- **Organization administrator, both variants (`organization_admin`, `organization_admin_no_bypass`), under `group` and `isolated`.** A by-id DELETE of a row the caller's read does not return is refused at the gate with the answer an id naming no row already got (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, "the assignment row to remove could not be read", details `{operation, object}`), and never reaches the engine. Before this head the same write was refused with guidance naming the row's organization. A row the caller reads is judged on what it read, so an own-organization row keeps its boundary guidance (pinned as a control for both variants and both tables). UPDATE, and the lifecycle verbs, are refused by the branch as "not part of the right" BEFORE any row is read, so their answers are identical for a hidden row and a missing id with or without this change — the tree bears out the body's claim that update answers are unchanged.
- **`single`.** No wall: the caller reads a row of another organization, so the guidance that names that organization stands. Consistent with the ruling (the row is one the caller can read); pinned as a control.
- **Tenant-level / platform administrator.** Returns from the gate before the branch; the engine answers both a hidden row and a missing id with its not-found (pinned as a control). Unchanged.
- **Delegate (no organization-administrator set).** Never enters the branch; judged by the delegated branch, whose pre-image read is unchanged (see ③).
- **A caller holding BOTH an organization-administrator set and a delegated scope.** The organization branch refuses as above, and `authorize` then hands the write to the delegated branch (`held.length > 0`), which answers it. That caller class is therefore still answered by the delegated branch — out of this PR by design (③).
- **System.** Short-circuits the middleware before the gate; a flow run's system context is refused ahead of it. Unchanged.
- **A caller read that is refused (declared 4xx) or that faults.** The gate has no catch, so it propagates; the middleware's `readDoorAnswerForGateRefusal` then asks the read door again and answers a declared read refusal as the answer for any id, and passes a fault (≥500) through as raised. Both are the same answers the merged by-id write door already gives that caller; a store fault is neither an answer nor a refusal, as `readRowById` already holds.

**`Clause-②: no` is right.** Every removal the branch admitted before is still admitted: admission requires the row to be the caller's own organization's and inside the boundary; both administrator sets hold `allowRead` on both assignment tables (the walled variant also `viewAllRecords`), the two objects declare no row-level sharing or owner floor that could hide an own-organization row, and the posture test's control reads another user's own-organization row for both variants under both walled postures. The only answers that change were refusals before and are refusals now, so nothing a consumer could do on `main` is taken away. The `canWrite` admission probe, which calls the gate with a synthetic context, answers `false` for that row before and after.

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@objectstack/plugin-security`; `Metadata-protocol: none`. No published schema, spec export, route or wire shape changes; the only observable change is the wording of one refusal for a class of write that was already refused. The changeset carries the rule, the two trailer lines and no mechanism.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **HTTP dogfood pin has no red leg.** The ablation was run only at the engine level (the posture test went 2 red, controls green, restored run green). The HTTP pin's ability to fail rests on its own controls: the wall is asserted active and not degraded, the caller is asserted no platform administrator and active in its organization, its GET of each foreign row is asserted 404 and of its own row 200, and the own-row control asserts the answer is NOT the missing-id answer. Accepted as a flag; the seat's follow-up should give the HTTP pin a measured red leg.
2. **The dogfood battery ran at the merge commit b6fe08a5, not this head.** Verified on the commit list: the two later commits (23da8f6, 51d9481) touch only the posture test. Accepted.
3. **Check-runs on this head.** Green: Auto Label, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, PR-body guards, Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test UI, Type Check · source gates, filter, Build Core, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI/release/engine gates, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Live E2E UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · workspace, Test Core 2/8, 3/8, 5/8, 6/8 and 7/8 (32 green at the last refresh). Skipped (opt-in or no UI change): 18.x upgrade harness, Build & E2E UI, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, the Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Lint UI, Packed-tarball smoke, Schedule gate, Temporal Conformance, Test UI shards, Type Check UI, UI Published Artifacts. STILL RUNNING at the time of this record: Test Core 1/8, 4/8 and 8/8. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; this PASS does not stand in for them. The Dogfood Regression Gate's three shards were skipped, so the new HTTP pin's CI execution on this head is not evidenced by a check-run.
4. **The delegated branch is left as it was — correctly, and escalated.** `materializeTargets` still reads a removal's pre-image under the system context and does not refuse an empty pre-image at the gate, so for a delegate — and for the organization administrator who also holds a delegated scope (①) — a hidden row and a missing id are not yet answered alike. Leaving it out of this PR is right: it is a different branch with its own pre-image semantics (a merged update image, subtree and allowlist judgments) and needs its own measurement. Escalated to the seat as its follow-up, no card.
5. **Unit harness.** `delegated-admin-gate.test.ts` (not in the diff) drives the organization branch through a fake engine that ignores context, so its foreign-row case now stands for a caller who reads the row and its expectation is unchanged — the same shape the `single` control pins on the real engine. Fine as is; a follow-up may add a context-honouring double.
6. **Docs.** The drift check names `content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx`; read at this head it states nothing about the pre-image's read context, so no sentence is contradicted. The lane may add the rule ("the removal is judged as the caller reads the row") when the delegated follow-up lands, so both branches are documented once.

### ④ Design judgment

Tried to break it against the cited code; no must-fix found.

- **An organization-administrator refusal still worded from a system read?** None. Update and the lifecycle verbs are refused before any read; a filter delete is refused before any read; insert judges payload rows. The branch's other reads (`positionBoundaryFailure`, `organizationBoundaryFailure`, `businessUnitInOrganization`) read the catalog and the organization's units by values taken from the row the caller read, and `businessUnitInOrganization` runs on `t.next` only (insert). No guidance about a removal's row can come from a read the caller did not make.
- **A caller read that throws something other than a declared 4xx.** The call passes only `where: { id }` (scalar by `extractSingleId`) and `context`, both accepted by `findOne` (`requireFindOnePredicate` is satisfied; no projection, no order). What can be thrown is a declared read refusal (answered, ①) or a store fault (propagated as raised, exactly as `readRowById` propagates one). The object-admission probe catches `PermissionDeniedError` only and lets a fault reach its outer deny-and-log, as before.
- **Cost on the admitted path.** Read count is unchanged (one gate read before, one now, plus the middleware's own step 2.7 pre-image read either way), but the gate's read now carries a full read-middleware pass as the caller, and it is not shared with the middleware's `opCtx.__preImage` memo, so an admitted by-id delete reads the row as the caller twice and a refused one three times (`readDoorAnswerForGateRefusal` asks again). Bounded (by id, `limit 1`), on a low-volume administrative write; not a must-fix. A follow-up may let the gate seed or consume that memo (the gate receives the middleware's own `opCtx`; the admission probe's synthetic context would be unaffected).
- **Race between the caller read and the write.** Unchanged window: the gate's read is advisory to the gate alone; the middleware's step 2.7 re-reads the row under the write-class filter and the tenant wall is composed into the write itself, so a row that changes organization after the gate read is refused there or written correctly, never written across the wall. The row-level answer is not an existence answer.
- **An own-organization row whose guidance changed.** None found: a readable row is judged on `organization_id`, `position` / the grant's set name, and (insert only) `business_unit_id`; neither set declares field masking on the two tables, and both controls show those fields present after the caller's read.
- **`single`.** The branch behaves as before: no wall, the row is read, the organization guidance stands; `callerOrganizationId` is the Default Organization. The control pins it for both variants.
- **Nested and on-behalf-of writes.** A nested by-id removal under the caller's context is now judged on the caller's read; a cross-wall row was refused before (with guidance) and is refused now (absent-row answer) — no admitted write is lost. An on-behalf-of write reads as the context the write carries, which is the principal the branch judges.
- **The test's precondition is the gate's own read.** `readAs` in the posture test issues the same `findOne` shape as `organizationTargets` and asserts it empty before comparing the write answers whole (status, code, sentence, details) and asserting the row is left; the HTTP pin compares whole bodies with only the caller-supplied id written out.
